pages.x: Timur was born near Samarkand into a Turkic-Mongol clan. Wounds in his youth left him lame in his right leg and arm, and his enemies called him Timur the Lame, Tamerlane. By 1370 he was master of the lands around Samarkand, ruling in the name of puppet khans descended from Genghis Khan.

Through the 1380s his armies swept over Persia, and cities that resisted were destroyed. When Isfahan rose against his garrison in 1387, his soldiers were ordered to bring in heads; a chronicler counted 70,000, piled into towers. Then he turned north and broke the Golden Horde, the Mongol khanate of the Russian steppe.

In 1398 Timur invaded India. Before the battle for Delhi he ordered his men to kill their Indian captives, fearing they would rise during the fight. He took the city, and for days his troops plundered and slaughtered. He left with elephants, treasure and craftsmen, and Delhi took a century to recover.

pages.x: In 1400 and 1401 he turned west, beat the Mamluks of Egypt, and sacked Aleppo and Damascus. Outside Damascus he talked for weeks with the great historian Ibn Khaldun, who had been let down the city wall on ropes to meet him. In Baghdad, which dared to resist, each soldier was ordered to bring back two heads.

In 1402 he met the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I, called the Thunderbolt, near Ankara. Bayezid's Tatar troops changed sides and his army broke. Bayezid was taken prisoner and died months later; later tales said he was carried about in an iron cage. The young Ottoman state almost fell apart.

In the winter of 1404 Timur, nearly seventy, set out to conquer Ming China. He fell ill on the march and died at Otrar in February 1405. His empire split among his sons and grandsons, but they ruled Central Asia for a century, and one of his descendants, Babur, founded the Mughal Empire in India.

Timur's wars may have killed 17 million people, one in twenty of everyone alive, though such figures are guesses. He was also a patron of builders and scholars, who made Samarkand one of the most beautiful cities in the world, with blue-tiled domes that still stand.
pts: From Delhi to Damascus in thirty-five years
He beat the Ottomans at Ankara in 1402
He made Samarkand a jewel of Asia
